request: how does a two-way table help you find a probability?

beats.intent: An empty two-way table: rows boys, girls, total; columns walk, bus, total
beats.narration: Thirty students say how they get to school. A two way table sorts them two ways at once: boy or girl, walk or bus.
beats.code:
stage.title("A two-way table")
w, h = 1.5, 0.65
tl = np.array([-6.2, 1.9, 0])
cell = lambda r, c: tl + np.array([(c + 0.5) * w, -(r + 0.5) * h, 0])
grid = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w, height=h, color=GREY_B, stroke_width=2).move_to(cell(r, c)) for r in range(4) for c in range(4)])
heads = VGroup(*[Text(t, font_size=24).move_to(cell(0, c)) for c, t in ((1, "walk"), (2, "bus"), (3, "total"))], *[Text(t, font_size=24).move_to(cell(r, 0)) for r, t in ((1, "boys"), (2, "girls"), (3, "total"))])
stage.play(Create(grid), FadeIn(heads))
stage.add(grid, heads)

beats.intent: The table filled in: boys 8 walk, 6 bus; girls 5 walk, 11 bus; totals 13, 17, 30
beats.narration: Eight boys walk and six take the bus; five girls walk and eleven take the bus. The totals are thirteen walkers, seventeen on the bus, thirty in all.
beats.code:
vals = {(1, 1): 8, (1, 2): 6, (1, 3): 14, (2, 1): 5, (2, 2): 11, (2, 3): 16, (3, 1): 13, (3, 2): 17, (3, 3): 30}
nums = VGroup(*[Text(str(v), font_size=28, color=YELLOW if 3 in rc else WHITE).move_to(cell(*rc)) for rc, v in vals.items()])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n) for n in nums], lag_ratio=0.1))
stage.add(nums)

beats.intent: The bus column boxed, 17 out of 30, and the girls-on-the-bus cell 11 picked out
beats.narration: Pick a student at random. Seventeen of the thirty take the bus. And of those seventeen on the bus, eleven are girls.
beats.code:
bus = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(grid[6], grid[10], grid[14]), color=ORANGE, buff=0.04)
gb = SurroundingRectangle(grid[10], color=GREEN, buff=0.08)
stage.play(Create(bus))
stage.play(Create(gb))
stage.add(bus, gb)
stage.label(bus, "17 of 30", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: The table beside P(bus) = 17/30 and P(girl, given bus) = 11/17
beats.narration: So the chance a random student takes the bus is seventeen thirtieths. The chance a bus rider is a girl is eleven out of seventeen.

request: where do impossible, unlikely, even and certain go on a probability scale?

beats.intent: A line from 0 to 1 marked impossible, even chance and certain
beats.narration: Probabilities go on a scale from nought to one. Nought is impossible, one is certain, and a half is an even chance.
beats.code:
stage.title("The probability scale")
nl = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 1, 0.25], length=10).move_to([0, -0.2, 0])
stage.play(Create(nl))
stage.add(nl)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(t, font_size=24).next_to(nl.n2p(v), DOWN, buff=0.3)) for v, t in ((0, "0 impossible"), (0.5, "1/2 even"), (1, "1 certain"))])

beats.intent: Rolling a 7 on a dice placed at 0, rolling a number from 1 to 6 placed at 1
beats.narration: Rolling a seven on an ordinary dice can't happen: nought. Rolling a number from one to six always happens: one.
beats.code:
e0 = Dot(nl.n2p(0), color=RED)
e1 = Dot(nl.n2p(1), color=GREEN)
stage.play(FadeIn(e0), FadeIn(e1))
stage.add(e0, e1)
stage.label(e0, "roll a 7", direction=UP, color=RED)
stage.label(e1, "roll 1 to 6", direction=UP, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: A six at 1/6, heads at 1/2 and not a six at 5/6 placed on the line
beats.narration: A six is unlikely, one in six. Heads on a coin is even, a half. Not rolling a six is likely, five in six.
beats.code:
evs = ((1 / 6, "a six", ORANGE), (0.5, "heads", BLUE), (5 / 6, "not a six", YELLOW))
for v, t, col in evs:
    d = Dot(nl.n2p(v), color=col)
    stage.play(FadeIn(d), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(d)
    stage.label(d, t, direction=UP, color=col)

beats.intent: The scale beside P(six) + P(not six) = 1/6 + 5/6 = 1
beats.narration: Something either happens or it doesn't, so the two chances add up to one.

request: if you roll a dice 60 times, how many sixes should you expect?

beats.intent: Dashed outline bars for faces 1 to 6, each at the expected 10
beats.narration: Roll a dice sixty times. Each face has a one in six chance, so you'd expect each about ten times.
beats.code:
stage.title("Expected number of sixes")
ax = Axes(x_range=[0, 7, 1], y_range=[0, 16, 4], x_length=6, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).move_to([-2.8, -0.5, 0])
stage.play(Create(ax))
stage.add(ax)
exp_bars = VGroup(*[DashedVMobject(Rectangle(width=0.6, height=ax.c2p(0, 10)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=GREY_B), num_dashes=24).move_to(ax.c2p(f, 5)) for f in range(1, 7)])
stage.play(Create(exp_bars))
stage.add(exp_bars)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("expected: 10 each", font_size=24, color=GREY_B).move_to(ax.c2p(3.5, 15))))

beats.intent: Bars for 60 real rolls filling in, each near 10 but not exactly
beats.narration: Now actually roll sixty times. The counts come out near ten, but not exactly: chance wobbles.
beats.code:
rolls = np.random.default_rng(1).integers(1, 7, size=60)
counts = [int((rolls == f).sum()) for f in range(1, 7)]
bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.5, height=ax.c2p(0, n)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7).move_to(ax.c2p(f, n / 2)) for f, n in zip(range(1, 7), counts)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromEdge(b, DOWN) for b in bars], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(bars)

beats.intent: The six bar highlighted: 11 sixes this time against the expected 10
beats.narration: This time there were eleven sixes, against the ten expected.
beats.code:
stage.play(bars[5].animate.set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.9).set_stroke(ORANGE))
stage.label(bars[5], f"{counts[5]} sixes", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: Expected frequency is the number of tries times the probability: sixty times a sixth, ten.

request: how do you estimate the mean from a grouped frequency table?

beats.intent: Bars for the heights of 20 students: 5 in 140-150 cm, 8 in 150-160, 7 in 160-170
beats.narration: Twenty students' heights are grouped: five between a hundred and forty and a hundred and fifty centimetres, eight between a hundred and fifty and a hundred and sixty, seven between a hundred and sixty and a hundred and seventy.
beats.code:
stage.title("Mean from grouped data")
ax = Axes(x_range=[140, 175, 10], y_range=[0, 10, 2], x_length=7, y_length=3.6, axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).move_to([-2.8, -0.6, 0])
stage.play(Create(ax))
stage.add(ax)
groups = ((145, 5, BLUE), (155, 8, GREEN), (165, 7, ORANGE))
bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=ax.c2p(150, 0)[0] - ax.c2p(140, 0)[0], height=ax.c2p(0, n)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=col, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(ax.c2p(m, n / 2)) for m, n, col in groups])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromEdge(b, DOWN) for b in bars], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(bars)
stage.label(ax, "height (cm)", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: A dot at the middle of each group: 145, 155, 165
beats.narration: We don't know each exact height, so treat everyone in a group as standing at its midpoint.
beats.code:
mids = VGroup(*[Dot(ax.c2p(m, n), color=YELLOW) for m, n, _ in groups])
stage.play(FadeIn(mids))
stage.add(mids)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(str(m), font_size=22, color=YELLOW).next_to(d, UP, buff=0.1)) for (m, n, _), d in zip(groups, mids)])

beats.intent: Each bar labelled with frequency × midpoint: 5 × 145, 8 × 155, 7 × 165
beats.narration: Five people at a hundred and forty five, eight at a hundred and fifty five, seven at a hundred and sixty five. That's three thousand one hundred and twenty centimetres altogether.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text(f"{n} × {m}", font_size=20).move_to(b)) for (m, n, _), b in zip(groups, bars)])
stage.label(bars, "total ≈ 3120 cm", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.narration: Divide by the twenty students: an estimated mean of a hundred and fifty six centimetres.
